gate_reason: Both design questions answered by Dalton in the Phase 2 interview (2026-08-03): keep the centered card + add a ✕ (dismiss hides both surfaces); dismissal persists the whole SPA session (no re-arm on state change; page reload clears it). No blockers, no blast-radius.
synthesis: The admin-only Bird's Eye Org Map (App.vue) shows a client-side notice when an org is active today (has scans) but no kit is reporting a live GPS position (DEV-2197). It renders as TWO sibling surfaces gated by the same `noKitsReporting` computed: a CENTERED card (pointer-events-none, no close) and a BOTTOM amber pill (pointer-events-auto, already non-blocking). The customer complaint targets the centered card — it reads as an undismissable modal obstructing the map center even though it doesn't block drags. Desired outcome: the admin can dismiss the notice; the map reads fully unobstructed after dismissal; the notice returns on a fresh occurrence of the condition or a new SPA session. No backend/data work — the trigger is already fully reactive client-side state.

scope.summary: Add a dismiss affordance to the 'No kits reporting GPS' notice and reconcile the two render sites (centered card + bottom pill) so the notice is dismissible, non-obstructive after dismissal, and reappears only on a fresh occurrence of the condition or a new SPA session. Single file: resources/js/clarity-scout/App.vue. No backend/data changes.

proposed_changes.change: Add a plain in-memory `noticeDismissed` ref (default false, component-scoped, NO persistence, NO watcher). Gate BOTH notice surfaces on `noKitsReporting && !noticeDismissed`.
proposed_changes.reason: Dalton (Phase 2): dismissal persists the whole SPA session — do NOT re-arm on state change. In-memory ref gives 'clears on next session' for free (App.vue remounts on page load). No watcher needed. AC1/AC2/AC4.

proposed_changes.change: Add a close ✕ button to the CENTERED card (37-48), mirroring Toast.vue's dismiss convention (aria-label="Dismiss", X SVG). Give the button `pointer-events-auto` (the card container stays pointer-events-none so the map remains draggable around the button); `@click` sets `noticeDismissed = true`. Because both surfaces gate on `!noticeDismissed`, one click hides the card AND the bottom pill together.
proposed_changes.reason: Dalton (Phase 2): keep the centered card, add a ✕; dismissing hides both surfaces. Preserves the DEV-2197 centered-explanation layout. Button-only pointer-events keeps AC2 (map interactive) maximal.

out_of_scope: Any backend/API change — trigger condition is fully client-side reactive.
Fixing the underlying GPS-feed gap (DEV-2197 root cause / sc_positions late/dropped writes).
Partial-GPS-loss detection (explicit future work in the DEV-2197 commit).
Rebuilding npm assets is a required mechanical ship step (public/build committed), not a scope item.

acceptance_criteria.item: User can dismiss the 'No kits reporting GPS' notice at any time
acceptance_criteria.reason: Neither surface (App.vue:37-48 card, 81-90 pill) has a close control today; add an explicit dismiss to the surviving surface(s).

acceptance_criteria.item: After dismissal, the map is fully interactive with no obstruction
acceptance_criteria.reason: Centered card is already pointer-events-none, but visually obstructs the center; dismissal must remove the visual obstruction.

acceptance_criteria.item: If the state changes and kits begin reporting GPS, the notice disappears automatically
acceptance_criteria.reason: Already satisfied by the reactive `noKitsReporting` computed (App.vue:330-336) driven by driverPositions via useBirdsEyePolling ~10s poll. Regression-guard: the new dismiss flag must not suppress the notice permanently.

acceptance_criteria.item: The notice does not re-appear until the next session or a meaningful state change
acceptance_criteria.reason: In-memory `noticeDismissed` ref, no watcher. Dalton chose session-scoped: once dismissed it stays hidden for the whole SPA session (does not re-arm even if kits report then go dark again). A page reload / new session resets it (fresh mount). Satisfies AC4's 'until the next session' branch.

questions.q: Which dismissal approach — (a) explicit close ✕, (b) auto-dismiss timeout (~10s), or (c) non-blocking banner/toast — or a combination?
questions.answer: (a) explicit close ✕ on the centered card (keep the card). Dismissing hides both the card and the bottom pill together.

questions.q: Keep the centered card (37-48) with a new ✕, or remove it and rely on the existing non-blocking bottom pill (81-90)?
questions.answer: Keep the centered card and add the ✕ to it (preserves the DEV-2197 centered-explanation layout). The bottom pill stays, gated on the same dismissed state.

questions.q: What counts as the AC4 'meaningful state change' that clears a prior dismissal?
questions.answer: Dalton chose the session branch of AC4 instead of the state-change branch: dismissal persists for the whole SPA session and only a page reload / new session clears it. No re-arm on a noKitsReporting false→true transition. (Code could have re-armed on that transition, but Dalton opted for simpler session-scoped behavior.)

questions.q: Persistence scope of the dismissal — in-memory vs localStorage/sessionStorage?
questions.answer: In-memory ref. sessionStorage is used nowhere in the repo; every localStorage dismiss (useInstallPrompt scanner_install_dismissed, useCollapsible) is a permanent cross-session preference — wrong shape for 'until next session'. In-memory ref reset on mount gives 'clears on next session' for free.

notes: DEV-2197 origin commit (5b6a7acbb) scoped the notice as full-dark only; partial GPS loss not detected — not touched here.
Both render sites are adminMode-gated (noKitsReporting requires mapStore.adminMode) — drivers never see this; no driver-side impact.

No existing composable implements a session-scoped, auto-resetting dismiss — useInstallPrompt/useCollapsible are permanent-until-changed localStorage patterns. This introduces a small new in-memory pattern.
npm run build + commit public/build/ required before ship (platform-commits-built-assets); no JS test runner.
